name: Pasargadae
description: Pasargadae, about 90 km northeast of Shiraz in southern Iran, was the first capital of the Persian Empire, founded by Cyrus the Great in the 6th century BC. Across its 160 hectares you can walk among the ruins of a gatehouse, audience hall and palace set in ancient gardens, climb the fortified terrace of Tall-e Takht, and stand before Cyrus's stone tomb.
